title: Name That Output! ARIA & Keyboard Conundrums 🎤

questions.question: What is the accessible name of this button?
questions.explanation: The `aria-label` attribute overrides the button's text content (the `×` icon) in the accessible name computation, so screen readers will announce 'Close, button'.

questions.question: What description is programmatically associated with this input via aria-describedby?
questions.codeSnippet: We'll never share your email.
questions.explanation: `aria-describedby` points to the ID of the element containing the hint. When the input is focused, screen readers may announce the label and then, after a pause, offer to read the description.

questions.question: What role does this element expose to assistive technology?
questions.explanation: The explicit `role="tab"` tells assistive tech that this element is a tab, even though it's built with a `<div>`.

questions.question: What state will be announced for this button when its controlled panel is visible?
questions.explanation: `aria-expanded='true'` is announced as 'expanded', indicating that the associated panel is currently open.

questions.question: What is the current value of this custom slider?
questions.explanation: The `aria-valuenow` attribute provides the current numeric value of the slider to screen readers.

questions.question: In the following DOM order, what element will receive focus first when the user presses the Tab key?
questions.explanation: Elements are added to the tab order according to their DOM position. The first `tabindex='0'` div appears before the other focusable elements, so 'First' gets focus initially.
